parsed.reason: Facts are all correct: tomorrow (Monday 26 October), start 15 h, end 16 h, and the Georgetown library. The 24-hour clock removes any AM/PM ambiguity. There is no invented detail, no inferred closure, and no filler. The title is kept as the event's name, not recast as a claim about the day. However, "il y a un jour de congé à la bibliothèque de Georgetown, jusqu'à 16 h" is clumsy. It reads as if a day off is happening at the library, which is a mild recasting of the title. A native speaker would not put a bare, unquoted title in as "un jour de congé" and would more naturally say "de 15 h à 16 h" instead of "à 15 h ... jusqu'à 16 h" split around the place. The text also has a stiff, readout feel with the formal "lundi 26 octobre" added to "demain". So it is capped at 3.
